guidance.heading: OUTLOOK
section: The company is reaffirming its full-year 2026 production and capital guidance with the Eagle Ford included through closing. For the fourth quarter of 2026, total production is expected to average between 1,660,000 and 1,700,000 Boe per day and oil production is expected to average between 550,000 and 560,000 barrels per day. Capital spending in the fourth quarter is expected to be between $1,290 million and $1,395 million.

Devon also provided an initial view of 2027. On a pro forma basis, adjusted for the Eagle Ford sale, the company expects 2027 oil production of approximately 525,000 barrels per day and total production of approximately 1,600,000 Boe per day on total capital of approximately $5.3 billion. Full 2027 guidance will be provided with fourth-quarter results in February.
Additional details of Devon’s forward-looking guidance are available on the company’s website at www.devonenergy.com.

desk.headline: Revenue up 58% to $6.9bn, in line; core EPS $1.42 beat; 2026 guidance reaffirmed, first 2027 outlook and faster buybacks

other.label: Production
other.change: vs 853 MBoe/d a year ago (Coterra merger)

results: Revenue rose 58% to $6.9bn, in line with estimates, as the first full quarter with Coterra almost doubled output to 1,668 MBoe/d.
Core EPS was $1.42, ahead of the $1.24 estimate; GAAP EPS was $0.88 after a $729m non-cash hedge valuation loss.
Adjusted free cash flow was $2.0bn; Devon paid $366m in dividends, bought back $414m of shares and repaid its last $750m term loan.
Cash costs of $12.89/Boe came in about 2% below the guidance midpoint; Eagle Ford oil volumes were weaker due to completion timing.
Devon agreed to sell its Eagle Ford assets for $4.2bn (about $3.5bn net, closing early 2027) and bought 25% of the Solitude gas pipeline.

guidance.summary: Devon kept its full-year 2026 production and capital guidance, set Q4 ranges and gave a first look at 2027 (after the Eagle Ford sale): oil of about 525,000 bbl/d on about $5.3bn of capital. It also raised its merger savings targets.

items.metric: Oil production (pro forma, ex Eagle Ford)

points: The CEO's letter says Devon sees strong value in its own shares; buybacks should top $1bn in Q4 and rise further in 2027.
The Eagle Ford sale was priced above Devon's own valuation of the asset, according to the letter.
About 75% of 2027 capital goes to the Permian, up from about 63% in 2026, with drilling on newly won federal acreage starting next year.
Devon expects low-single-digit oil growth on roughly flat capital, and to cut gross debt to $9bn in early 2027.
Technology such as automated gas lift and longer laterals is credited for better capital efficiency.
